links.title: Chapter 1: Python Basics - the lecture deck for this chapter
links.why: The slides this chapter is taught from: 59 slides, each with its talk track in the speaker notes. It sits in the chapter's own folder, one level above this page, and is renewed from the same research record and executed examples the page draws on.

links.title: 3. An Informal Introduction to Python
links.why: Worked examples of int and float arithmetic, / versus //, and string joining and repeating.

links.title: 6. Expressions
links.why: The formal rules for arithmetic operators, including the operator precedence table.

links.title: Built-in Types
links.why: Reference for int, float and str, including the + and * operations on sequences.

links.title: Built-in Functions
links.why: Reference entries for print, input, len, int, float and str, with signatures.

links.title: 7. Input and Output
links.why: Tutorial on formatting output and using print, including formatted string literals with examples.

links.title: 2. Lexical analysis
links.why: The language reference section on f-strings: replacement fields, format specifiers and the = debug specifier.

links.title: PEP 498 – Literal String Interpolation
links.why: The design proposal that introduced f-strings in Python 3.6, with its motivation and rules.

links.title: 1. Command line and environment
links.why: How to start the interpreter, enter interactive mode with -i, and the command-line options.

links.title: 2. Using the Python Interpreter
links.why: Tutorial on invoking the interpreter, the >>> and ... prompts, and interactive mode.

links.title: Python support for free threading
links.why: How to install a free-threaded build and check whether the GIL is disabled.

links.title: PEP 703 – Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython
links.why: The proposal behind the free-threaded build: what changes inside CPython and its cost for single-threaded code.

links.title: What's new in Python 3.14
links.why: Release highlights for 3.14, including free-threaded support, template strings and the improved interactive shell.

links.title: venv — Creation of virtual environments
links.why: How to create and activate an isolated environment with python -m venv.

links.title: Installing Python modules
links.why: How to install, pin and upgrade packages with python -m pip.
